title: Scaling Up the Training Loop
summary: The part 2 loop trains a byte-level toy. This lesson turns it into a loop you can leave running for hours: a trained BPE tokenizer, gradient accumulation, mixed precision with autocast and a gradient scaler, a warmup-plus-cosine schedule, resumable checkpoints and logging you can trust. Each change is shown as working PyTorch with the arithmetic behind it and the quiet bugs it can introduce.
objectives: Compute what a BPE vocabulary costs in embedding, LM-head and logits memory, and convert per-token loss to bits per byte
Implement gradient accumulation, compute the effective batch, and explain why the loss is divided by the number of micro-batches
Write a correct FP16 or BF16 training step with autocast and GradScaler, including unscaling before gradient clipping
Implement warmup with cosine decay per optimizer step and evaluate the learning rate at any step
List everything a resumable checkpoint must hold, estimate its size, and read loss, learning-rate, gradient-norm and throughput curves to diagnose a run
prerequisites: You should have the simple training loop from [Train a Tiny GPT](/learn/model-foundations/train-a-tiny-gpt) and the model from [The Modern Architecture](/learn/model-foundations/modern-architecture), which this lesson trains. The theory behind the pieces lives elsewhere and is not repeated: byte-pair encoding and vocabulary size in [Tokenization](/learn/model-foundations/tokenization), and number formats, memory per parameter and learning-rate schedules in [Training at Scale](/learn/training-and-adaptation/training-at-scale).
